newsitem.title: USA: Calif. officials announce Shasta Lake project.
newsitem.headline: Calif. officials announce Shasta Lake project.

text.p: Knauf Fiber Glass plans to build a $100 million facility in Shasta Lake, Calif., the largest manufacturing expansion in northern California in recent years, state and local officials said on Tuesday.

Jim Zauher, general manager of the Economic Development Corp of Shasta County, said the plant would provide more than 150 jobs in an area that has suffered from one of the highest unemployment rates in the state.
Construction of the $100 million facility was scheduled to begin during the summer of 1997. The plant was expected to open in late 1998.
State officials said the privately-held Knauf Fiber Glass is a $300 million a year manufacturer of commercial, industrial and residential insulation products.

The California Trade and Commerce Agency said the company decided to locate in Shasta Lake over a competing site in Medford, Oregon. Officials said the company decided to expand in California in part because of the enterprise tax credits.
